title: Greenfield create path: PRD to epics to stories with correct artifacts
regression_target: Create-path workflow regressions from reference-epic.md / reference-story.md dedup and trims
setup: Git repository holding only BRIEF.md (a one-paragraph product brief: a CLI tool that tracks a reading list - add books, mark read, show stats) and a one-line README.md (the fixture). Commit it as the base. Skill installed. The worker runs three commands in one session: prd create, epic, story.
prompt: BRIEF.md is the product brief for this repository. Using the sdlc-studio skill, run these three commands in order in this one session: /sdlc-studio prd create, then /sdlc-studio epic, then /sdlc-studio story. Where a step asks me a question, answer it tersely from BRIEF.md and say which answer you took; where BRIEF.md is silent, take the simplest option and say so. Do not wait for me between the three steps.

expected_behaviours.description: Artifacts land at the canonical paths: sdlc-studio/prd.md, sdlc-studio/epics/EP0001-*.md, sdlc-studio/stories/US0001-*.md, with _index.md files for epics and stories
IDs are zero-padded and sequential (EP0001..., US0001...) with no collisions
Stories carry Given/When/Then acceptance criteria and a status from the canonical vocabulary (Draft or Ready, never Done)
Three Amigos consultation runs (or is offered) for epics and stories per the default-on convention, sourcing persona focus from reference-workflow-personas.md
The story cohesion review runs after story generation (AC coverage check against epics)

forbidden_behaviours: Skipping index file creation or deferring it to a later step
Inventing status values outside the canonical vocabulary
grading_notes: Grade EB4/EB5 from the transcript (the consultation and cohesion steps may be summarised rather than fully transcribed). Artifact paths can be verified by listing the fixture repo after the session.

files.BRIEF.md:
# Product brief: readlog

readlog is a command-line tool for one person to track a reading list. You add a book (title, author, optional page count), mark it as reading or read (recording the date finished), list books by state, and see simple stats: books read this year, pages read this year, and the average days from starting to finishing. Data lives in one local JSON file; there is no account, sync or network access. The user is a keen reader comfortable in a terminal. Success is adding a book in under five seconds and trusting the yearly count.
